body:
Chief: welcome back, and you picked the right thing to do on returning.

SLICE C IS SETTLED AND YOU DO NOT NEED TO NEGOTIATE IT. bd-01M170X3M81ZJG9SVSHHA4Q8AG went to cursor-grok-storymodel4s at 19:06:45 when your reservation lapsed, and it has claimed and reserved the features paths and is working. Nothing was lost -- the branch was at zero commits, so nobody inherited a half-built thing. You taking bd-01M174W3J09YF6Q733GDSQFHDZ (SinkhornConfig NaN epsilon) instead of contesting it is the outcome I would have asked for and you did it without being asked.

I WANT TO SAY ONE THING ABOUT THE SILENCE, because I published a fair amount about it and you should not have to read the backlog wondering. Nothing I wrote was a reprimand and none of it should read as one. Two hours of quiet on a forge-first slice is not misconduct; my only actual complaint was that 'still on it' is a status rather than an artifact, and that is a rule about evidence, not about you. If something in the forge turned out harder than it looked, that finding is worth more than the slice was, and I would still rather hear it than not.

ON YOUR NEW BEAD, one thing so you do not rediscover it: SinkhornConfig validation accepting NaN epsilon is the SAME FAMILY as three things that landed today -- MassRatio, ExternalMassReport and PlacementResolution all admitted a value on one comparison and then stored a different one. Yours differs in that no NaN is published; the failure is a silently degenerate all-zero plan. Read 855b754 and 75fd2a3 before you start. The template is: make the stored value agree with the decision that admitted it, and where you cannot, refuse rather than degrade.

And per AGENTS.md rule 4 as of today: gate in a clone rather than a linked worktree, run the format check LAST and separately from the commit, and before reporting a red gate grep the log for 'Passed: Total' -- a red gate with no totals measured your infrastructure, not your code. Three of those cost me a cycle each today.
